summary: Explains optional module utilities: module_utils imports nested inside if or try blocks are treated as optional by the payload builder and omitted if missing, while missing top-level imports fail the build, illustrated with respawn (2.11+).
questions: How can my collection module use new ansible-core features but still run on older versions?
Why does my module fail to build on Ansible 2.10 when importing respawn?
Does Ansible treat imports inside try blocks differently?

answer_card.title: Optional module_utils imports
answer_card.answer_md:
The payload builder treats any `module_utils` import nested in a block (`if`, `try`) as **optional**: if not found, it's left out and your code must handle the absence. A missing **top-level** import fails the payload build.

E.g. `from ansible.module_utils.common.respawn import respawn_module` fails on Ansible ≤ 2.10 unless wrapped in `try/except ImportError`.
